preconditions.description: The number of objects n is an integer between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(type_list) == n and all(t in {0, 1} for t in type_list) and any(t == 1 for t in type_list)
preconditions.description: The type_list is a list of length n where each element is 0 (mountain) or 1 (hotel), and at least one hotel exists.

preconditions.expression: len(a_list) == n and all(0 <= a <= n for a in a_list)
preconditions.description: The a_list is a list of length n where each element is an integer between 0 and n inclusive, representing ski tracks (0 means no incoming track).

preconditions.expression: all(a_list[i] == 0 or type_list[a_list[i] - 1] == 0 for i in range(n))
preconditions.description: No hotel (type 1) has an outgoing ski track (a_i ≠ 0 implies type_{a_i} = 0).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().split() == [str(k)] + path and k == len(path) and all(1 <= v <= n for v in path)
postconditions.description: The first line of stdout is the integer k (path length), and the second line is a space-separated list of k integers representing the path v_1, ..., v_k.

postconditions.expression: all(type_list[v - 1] == 0 for v in path[:-1]) and type_list[path[-1] - 1] == 1
postconditions.description: All objects in the path except the last are mountains (type 0), and the last object is a hotel (type 1).

postconditions.expression: all(a_list[path[i] - 1] == path[i + 1] for i in range(k - 1))
postconditions.description: For each consecutive pair in the path, there is a ski track from v_i to v_{i+1} (a_{v_i} = v_{i+1}).

postconditions.expression: not any(k < len(p) and all(type_list[p[i] - 1] == 0 for i in range(len(p) - 1)) and type_list[p[-1] - 1] == 1 and all(a_list[p[i] - 1] == p[i + 1] for i in range(len(p) - 1)))
postconditions.description: The path length k is maximal: no other path satisfies the conditions with a longer length.
